---
title: Network glossary
department: logistics
status: current
---
Terms used across the operational documentation. Where a definition here
conflicts with a definition in a process page, this glossary wins and the
process page is corrected.

Backhaul — a return leg that carries revenue freight instead of running empty. A
backhaul is priced separately from the outbound leg.

Deadhead — a linehaul leg run with no freight aboard. A deadhead is scheduled
only to reposition equipment, and every deadhead needs approval from network
control before it is added to the plan.

Drop trailer — a trailer left at a site for loading and collected on a later
visit rather than waiting for the load to be completed.

Induction — the point at which freight enters the sortation network and receives
its first scan.

Linehaul — a scheduled movement between two network sites, distinct from the
first and last legs of a journey.

Rollover — a load left behind when a wave reaches capacity. A rollover is held
for the next wave, and network control owns the rollover until it moves.

Tender — the act of handing freight over to the carrier. The tender timestamp is
what the commitment is measured from.

Wave — a scheduled batch of work released to the floor at a fixed time.
